title: TaqMan Array Card for Enteropathogen Detection
author: Jie Liu
materials: Equipment preparation. Ensure that the correct TaqMan Array Card block, heated cover, and loading tray are installed. Turn on the instrument and then the computer. Open the ViiA 7 or QuantStudio software programs as appropriate. Ensure that the computer is communicating properly with the instrument Click on the Instrument Console. When the computer properly connects with the instrument, the instrument icon will have a green check.

Bead beating . Bead beat at maximum speed for 2-3 minutes (instrument dependent, see below). Incubatethe suspension for 5 min at 95°C. Vortex for 15 s then centrifuge sample at full speed (approximately 20,000g) for 1 min to pellet the stool particles. Note: Bead disruption for too long will overheat the sample and cause nucleic acid degradation, too little time is ineffective and will not enhance the extraction of DNA. Care should be taken in determining bead beating time for the instrument used. If immediately after bead beating the tube is hot, decrease the time. E.g., for Fastprep FP120 from Bio101 Thermo Electronic Corporation (Fisher NC9646109) - Bead disruption at maximum speed for 3 minutes is sufficient without over heating the preparation; For BioSpec Mini-Beadbeater (BioSpec 693, Mini-Beadbeater-8) - Bead disruption at maximum speed for 2 minutes is sufficient.
Name the experiment (the software automatically generates the name by date and time).

steps.title: Prepare External Control Working Solution
steps.instruction: Reconstitute the lyophilized external control (MS2 and PhHV mix).

substeps.instruction: Quickly spin the vial to bring the pellet to the bottom.
Add 50 µl of standard diluent to each vial and mix well.
Use 1 µl per sample extraction.
Store leftover solution at -80°C (do not use if frozen-thawed more than twice).

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the InhibitEX buffer and supplement with external control.

substeps.instruction: Shake InhibitEX Buffer thoroughly; if precipitate exists, incubate at 37-70°C for ~15 minutes until dissolved.
Prepare fresh daily for N+1 samples: mix 1 ml InhibitEX buffer with 1 µl external control working solution per sample (e.g., 11 ml buffer + 11 µl control for 10 samples).

steps.title: Sample Aliquoting and Bead Addition
steps.instruction: Prepare specimen tubes with appropriate sample volumes and beads.

substeps.instruction: For fecal samples: weigh 180–220 mg stool (or 200 µl if liquid) into a 2 ml screw top bead-beater compatible tube.
For rectal swabs: snap off the shaft and store the bottom flocked portion frozen in a 2 ml screw top bead-beater compatible tube.
Include one blank negative control per extraction batch.
Add ~370 mg (one eppendorf tube capful) of acid-washed glass beads (212-300 µm, 50-70 U.S. sieve, Sigma G1277) to stool, flocked swab tip, or blank tube.

steps.title: Lysis and Protease Treatment
steps.instruction: Lyse the samples and treat with proteinase K.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 ml of the InhibitEX/external control solution to each specimen tube (or blank) and vortex for 1 min.
Pipet 25 μl of proteinase K into a new 2 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Pipet 600 μl supernatant from the lysis step into the tube containing proteinase K (do not transfer solid material; centrifuge again if necessary).
Add 600 μl Buffer AL (do not add proteinase K directly to Buffer AL).
Vortex for 15 s to homogenize.
Incubate at 70°C for 10 min.
Centrifuge briefly to remove drops from the tube lid.

steps.title: Purification via Spin Column
steps.instruction: Purify nucleic acids using QIAamp spin columns.

substeps.instruction: Add 600 μl of ethanol (96–100%) to the lysate and vortex.
Centrifuge briefly to clear the lid.
Label a QIAamp spin column and place it in a 2 ml collection tube.
Apply 600 μl of lysate to the column (avoid moistening the rim) and centrifuge at full speed for 1 min.
Transfer the column to a new 2 ml collection tube and discard the filtrate.
Repeat the application and centrifugation two more times until all lysate (~1800 μl total) has passed through the column.

steps.title: Wash the Spin Column
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane to remove contaminants.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 μl Buffer AW1 (ensure 25 ml ethanol 96–100% was added to concentrate before first use) to the column, centrifuge at full speed for 1 min, and discard filtrate.
Add 500 μl Buffer AW2 (ensure 30 ml ethanol 96–100% was added to concentrate before first use) to the column, centrifuge at full speed for 3 min, and discard filtrate.
Place the column in a new 2 ml collection tube and centrifuge at full speed for 3 min to eliminate Buffer AW2 carryover.

steps.title: Elute and Store Total Nucleic Acid
steps.instruction: Elute the TNA and aliquot for storage.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the column to a labeled microcentrifuge tube.
Pipet 200 μl Buffer ATE directly onto the membrane.
Incubate for 1-3 min at room temperature, then centrifuge at full speed for 1 min.
Pipet 100 μl of the extracted TNA into two separate storage tubes.
Store at -70 to –80°C.

steps.title: Prepare qPCR Reaction Mix
steps.instruction: Prepare the master mix and individual reaction tubes.

substeps.instruction: Prepare master mix for 8 samples: 425 µL Ag-Path-ID 2XRT-PCR buffer and 34 µL Ag-Path-ID Enzyme mix.
Aliquot 54 µL of master mix into eight 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Add the following to each tube: 20 µL TNA extract from stool + 26 µL nuclease-free water, OR 46 µL TNA extract from rectal swabs, OR extraction blanks, OR nuclease-free water (for NTC).
Mix gently and centrifuge to remove air bubbles.

steps.title: Configure Software Experiment
steps.instruction: Set up the run parameters in the software.

substeps.instruction: Set up a new experiment 'From Template' using the lot-specific template.
Confirm properties: Array Card Block, Standard Curve, TaqMan Reagents, Standard.
Define and name the samples.
Confirm Cycling Conditions: RT (1 cycle) 45°C for 20min; Denaturation (1 cycle) 95°C for 10min; PCR (40 cycles) 95°C for 15sec and 60°C for 1min (data collection).
Save the experiment.

steps.title: Load the TaqMan Array Card
steps.instruction: Load the PCR reaction mix into the TAC cards.

substeps.instruction: Allow TAC cards to reach room temperature in original packaging.
Place card foil side down on the bench.
Slowly dispense 100 µL of PCR reaction mix into the fill port at an angle, sweeping the mix around the reservoir toward the vent port without introducing bubbles.

steps.title: Centrifuge the TaqMan Array Card
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the cards to ensure wells are filled.

substeps.instruction: Set bucket type: 15679 (Previous-Gen) or 3618 (Current-Gen).
Insert card into array holder with reservoirs projecting upwards and reaction wells facing the 'This Side Out' label.
Fill remaining holder positions with blank or used arrays.
Place holder in bucket with 'This Side Out' label facing the front of the bucket.
Balance the centrifuge with four buckets.
Centrifuge for two consecutive 1-min spins.
Remove cards and inspect filling. If excess mix remains in the reservoir, centrifuge for 1 additional minute (do not exceed 1200 rpm or 3 min total centrifugation).

steps.title: Seal the TaqMan Array Card
steps.instruction: Use the sealer to isolate the card wells.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the sealer carriage is in the starting position.
Orient card foil side up with fill ports farthest from you and rear pin groves aligned to stylus pins.
Secure the card with spring clips and push until seated level with the sealer base.
Push the carriage slowly and steadily in the direction of the 'Push to stake' arrow until it reaches the mechanical stops.
Remove the card and inspect for proper sealing (indentations must match main channels).
Return the carriage to the starting position.

steps.title: Final Card Preparation and Run
steps.instruction: Trim the card and start the instrument run.

substeps.instruction: Trim off the fill reservoirs using scissors, using the card carrier edge as a guide.
Place the sealed card in the instrument: well A1 at top left, notched corner at top right, barcode facing front.
In software, click 'Run', select the instrument, and click 'START RUN'.
